source.title: The effect of Target Normalization and Momentum on Dying ReLU
source.authors: Isac Arnekvist; J. Carvalho; D. Kragic; J. A. Stork

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports regression training results on UCI datasets and analyzes dead ReLUs in single-unit and deeper networks, a different setting from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports regression MSE and dead-ReLU outcomes, not classification training error on CIFAR benchmarks or the specific outcomes named in V1–V6. Its results are recorded as findings for none of the listed versions. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures regression fit, dead-ReLU incidence and single-unit convergence under target scaling and momentum. These do not measure any version's specified outcome: classification training error, width-dependent spurious minima, initialization-dependent training speed or depth, stability-threshold recovery, or batch-normalization training speed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors motivate target normalization, connect momentum-induced oscillations to dying ReLUs through affine-system analysis and approximate single-ReLU dynamics, and find greater susceptibility in deeper regression networks, including residual networks with batch normalization. Their deeper-network experiments report no additional ReLU death during SGD optimization.
record.recipe_differences: Regression with mean-squared error on UCI datasets and analytical or numerical dead-ReLU analysis; not the benchmark classification-training recipes in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Target variance and bias, momentum, optimizer, and architecture depth affect the reported fit or dead-ReLU outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Regression fit worsens as target scale departs from one or target mean departs from zero; small target scale increases dead-ReLU incidence with Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Target normalization affects regression fitting and, together with momentum optimization, susceptibility to dying ReLUs.

fits_no_version.finding: At gamma = 10^-4, deeper networks exhibit more and faster ReLU death during Adam training, including residual networks with batch normalization. SGD produces no additional dead units during optimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth can aggravate momentum-associated dying ReLUs in regression, even with residual connections and batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: At gamma = 0.001 and eta = 0.1, increasing momentum beyond approximately 0.7 leaves only small initialization regions converging to the optimum; without momentum, most tested initializations converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small target scale and oscillatory momentum dynamics can drive a single ReLU into a practically inactive region.

record.problems: The empirical work concerns regression on four UCI datasets rather than classification benchmarks. Several outcomes are shown only in figures, and the deeper-network summary is averaged over four datasets; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results were omitted. Figure-only results are retained without reconstructing numerical values.

untested.parts: All: CIFAR classification training error, random labels, model size and training recipes.
All: spurious local minima as teacher/student widths grow and the effect of extra student neurons.
All: depth-dependent classification training error, identity-shortcut prevention and special initialization exceptions.
All: activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal/Gaussian comparisons.
All: learning rates relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature changes, recovery and edge-of-stability training.
All: batch-normalization effects on accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because their measures do not establish those versions; this does not deny the reported dying-ReLU effects. The study cites original sources concerning initialization and batch normalization but does not independently test their version-specific claims.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification, corrupted or random labels, model size, and early stopping or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual classification training error on ImageNet or CIFAR-10, shortcut effects on training error, and the named special initializations.
Activation-matched initializations, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer plain CNN training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness behavior.
Batch normalization effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: NN used for regression (architecture in Eq. 33)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam while target variance and bias were varied; fit measured on a training-set subset.
rows.note: Text says fit degrades as target variance deviates from 1 or target mean deviates from 0. Figure 1 provides values only graphically; no exact values transcribed.
rows.check: Regression MSE does not measure a listed version. Appendix A specifies evaluation after 250,000 updates and eight seeds. Gamma is a target scale (standard deviation after normalization), so target variance is gamma squared.

rows.subject: NN used for regression (architecture in Eq. 33)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD while target variance and bias were varied; fit measured on a training-set subset.
rows.note: Text states that decreasing target variance leads to more dying ReLUs only with momentum optimization, and the paper reports that SGD does not produce more dead ReLUs during optimization in its deeper-network experiments. MSE values are figure-only.
rows.check: A separate SGD MSE result is not established by the supplied text. Figure 1 distinguishes Adam and SGD for dead-ReLU incidence; Appendix A specifies Adam for the regression experiment. Remove this row unless an SGD MSE series can be verified.

rows.subject: NN used for regression (architecture in Eq. 33)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam while target variance was varied; dead-ReLU proportion measured.

conditions.value: four datasets: Airfoil, Facebook, Real Estate, Superconduct

rows.note: The text says decreasing target variance leads to more dying ReLUs only with momentum optimization. Figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Dead-ReLU incidence does not measure a listed version. Separate Figure 1's shallow-network scale sweep from Figure 6's deeper-network experiment at gamma = 10^-4; the latter duplicates R4/R5. Gamma denotes target scale, not variance.

rows.subject: Multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained at different depths and with Adam or SGD; dead-ReLU proportion tracked over gradient steps.
rows.measure: Proportion of dead ReLUs in the layer with the highest ratio
rows.note: Authors state that ReLUs die more often and faster as architecture depth increases. The plotted numerical values are figure-only.
rows.check: Dead-ReLU proportion cannot establish V3's training-error degradation. Split Adam and SGD conditions: increasing depth aggravates dying during Adam training, whereas the authors explicitly report no additional dying during SGD optimization. Distinguish dead units at initialization from units dying during training.

rows.subject: Residual NN (with batch norm.)
rows.operation_detail: Trained at different depths and with Adam or SGD; dead-ReLU proportion tracked over gradient steps.
rows.measure: Proportion of dead ReLUs in the layer with the highest ratio
rows.note: Authors state that dying ReLU is aggravated in deeper architectures, even for residual networks with batch normalization. The plotted numerical values are figure-only.
rows.check: Dead-ReLU proportion establishes neither V3's training-error comparison nor V6's training-speed comparison. Split Adam and SGD conditions. Batch normalization prevents initially dead units in these residual networks, but additional dying occurs during Adam optimization; SGD does not produce additional dead units.

rows.subject: Single-ReLU model
rows.operation_detail: Numerically followed gradient-descent parameter updates from initial coordinates until update norm fell below 10^-6; compared target variance and momentum settings.

conditions.value: β varied; oscillation expected for β > 0.7

rows.measure: Convergence to global optimum versus dead cone
rows.note: Text says most initializations still converged to the ground truth without momentum; with momentum and small γ = 0.001, dying ReLU increased and only small initialization regions converged to the global optimum. The plotted regions are figure-only.
rows.check: Single-unit convergence regions are outside V2's width-dependent spurious-local-minimum claim; the authors describe dead-cone critical points as saddles. The numerical trajectories use approximate gradients derived with an affine target. Separate no-momentum/beta ≤ 0.7 conditions from beta > 0.7 at small gamma.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
